```gherkin
Feature: Event Log Storage and Content

  Scenario: GUI stores event log in non-volatile memory
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user confirms ventilation settings
    Then the event log is stored in non-volatile memory

  Scenario: Event log includes all confirmed ventilation settings
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user confirms ventilation settings
    Then the event log includes all confirmed ventilation settings

  Scenario: Event log includes date and timestamp
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user confirms ventilation settings
    Then the event log includes a date and timestamp

  Scenario: Event log includes changes to system's real time clock
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user changes the system's real time clock
    Then the event log includes the current date/time followed by the new date/time

  Scenario Outline: Event log includes confirmed ventilation settings with different values
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user confirms ventilation settings with <settings>
    Then the event log includes all confirmed ventilation settings with <settings>

    Examples:
      | settings        |
      | Normal          |
      | High            |
      | Low             |
      | Invalid setting |

  Scenario Outline: Event log includes date and timestamp with different dates
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user confirms ventilation settings
    Then the event log includes a date and timestamp with <date>

    Examples:
      | date       |
      | 2022-01-01 |
      | 2022-12-31 |
      | 2022-01-01 00:00:00 |
      | 2022-12-31 23:59:59 |

  Scenario Outline: Event log includes changes to system's real time clock with different dates
    Given the system is in a normal operating state
    When the user changes the system's real time clock to <new_date>
    Then the event log includes the current date/time followed by the new date/time with <new_date>

    Examples:
      | new_date       |
      | 2022-01-01     |
      | 2022-12-31     |
      | 2022-01-01 00:00:00 |
      | 2022-12-31 23:59:59 |

```
